title: Paint Fence
summary: Given n posts and k colors, calculate the number of ways to paint the fence such that no three consecutive posts have the same color, with each post painted exactly once.
statement: Given n posts and k colors, calculate the number of ways to paint the fence such that no three consecutive posts have the same color, with each post painted exactly once.
constraints: 1≤n≤50 and 1≤k≤1000. The number of valid paintings fits a signed 32-bit integer.
Each of n fence posts receives one of k colors. Return the number of assignments with no three consecutive posts sharing one color.
hints: Classify a valid prefix by whether its last two colors are equal or different.
Appending a different color to either state gives k-1 choices; appending the same color is allowed only after a different ending.
The combined recurrence is ways[i]=(ways[i-1]+ways[i-2])·(k-1), with bases k and k².
When k=1, only lengths one and two are valid; the recurrence naturally gives zero afterward.
editorial: A valid painting ending with two equal colors must have had a different color immediately before that pair. Separating same-ending and different-ending states produces the combined recurrence (previous one plus previous two) times k-1. Two scalar totals are enough. The independent checker uses the same counting definition, while exhaustive regression enumerates every small color assignment to verify the recurrence separately.

tests.explanation: There are 2^3=8 colorings of three posts; the two all-equal colorings are invalid, leaving 6.
One post may use any of the three colors, so there are 3 valid paintings.
